en: I worship Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, the descendant of Bhṛgu and son of Reṇukā, who holds an axe and a bow in his two hands and is the destroyer of the Kṣatriyas. 1.
I bow to Rāma of the Bhṛgu lineage, the delighter of Reṇukā’s heart, who liberated her from distress, the destroyer of [the demon] Utpāta, and the annihilator of the Kṣatriyas. 2.
Devoted to protecting his own kin who were afflicted by fear, dedicated to righteousness,
free from pride, and beloved— such was the son of Jamadagni, esteemed as a hero.
He had brought Mahādeva under his control, was the destroyer of haughty royal lineages,
possessed great splendor, was the slayer of Kārtavīrya, and the destroyer of worldly existence.
Holding an axe in his right hand and a bow in his left,
the beautiful ornament of the Bhṛgu lineage is dark as a rain cloud and captivating to the mind.
To the pure and awakened one, the great scholar of wisdom, the expert in battle, to Rāma, the vessel of Śrīdatța’s compassion, who delights the brahmins; ||6||
He who recites these names of the Lord—which dry up the ocean of worldly seeking, which are purifying, and which grant long life—shall become perfected. (7)
Thus ends the Śrī Paraśurāma Stotra, composed by the venerable Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
